paras: The lynching of an unknown man near Jacksboro, Texas, came to light on March 19, 1881, when his body was found hanging by the neck with nine bullet holes in Howard Valley, nine miles from the town. He was said to be a horse thief, and his killers were not identified. A single Jacksboro dispatch carried the case to newspapers from Virginia to Nevada, two of which headed it "LYNCHED."

According to the dispatch, dated Jacksboro, March 19, the dead body of an unknown man, "supposed to be a horse-thief," was found that day in Howard Valley. He was hanging by the neck, and his body contained nine bullet holes. The Dallas Daily Herald added that he hung from the limb of a tree. No report gives his name or race, the number of men who killed him, or when or where he had been seized.
The dispatch closed with the statement that "the executioners are unknown," and no report of an inquest, arrest or further inquiry appears in the coverage.

The item originated as a Jacksboro special to the St. Louis Republican, as the Gold Hill Daily News and the Sacramento Daily Record-Union credited it. On March 20 the Chicago Daily Tribune ran it under the one-word head "LYNCHED," while the Memphis Daily Appeal titled it "The Texas Fashion" in a column of crime news called "Some Hard Cases." The St. Paul Daily Globe cut it to a brief ending "Supposed horsethief. Executioners unknown," and the Staunton Spectator, reprinting it under "LYNCHED," placed it at "Jacksborough, Mo."

The one Texas paper in the coverage, the Dallas Daily Herald, gave the story a line in its "Texas Topics" column on March 24. It dropped the horse-thief supposition and ended with the remark, "He was tolerably dead." Late in March a shorter version, describing a body "riddled with bullets" found hanging from a tree "on the 19th," circulated in weekly news summaries in Tennessee, Arkansas and Missouri. None of the papers commented on the killing beyond these headlines and asides.

chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A man said to be a horse thief was found hanged and shot by unknown 'executioners', and the dispatch ran under the head 'LYNCHED' (A1, A2, A8).

The man was killed by hanging and nine gunshots by unknown 'executioners', with no lawful authority reported, and he was 'supposed to be a horse thief', a crime-punishment pretext (A1, A2, A9). No report gives the number of killers, so a group of three or more is implied by the hanging and nine bullets but not stated.
Every report traces to one Jacksboro dispatch credited to the St. Louis Republican (A1, A2, A5); the Dallas Herald's brief (A9) adds only the tree limb and may rest on the same report.

accounts.gist: An unknown man was found hanging from a tree limb with nine bullet holes near Jacksboro 'a few days ago'; no accusation given.

framing.detail: Northern dailies ran the dispatch as a one-paragraph item under 'LYNCHED' or folded it into news briefs.
The Memphis Daily Appeal headed it 'The Texas Fashion', casting the killing as a regional habit, within a column titled 'Some Hard Cases'.
The Dallas Daily Herald dropped the horse-thief label and closed with the quip 'He was tolerably dead.'

conflicts.note: The Staunton Spectator's 'Mo.' is evidently a copying error; every other version, including the Texas paper, places it in Texas.

versions.value: 'to-day' in a dispatch dated March 19 / 'Saturday' / 'on the 19th'

conflicts.note: Consistent: the Dallas column ran March 24, five days after the dated dispatch.
